questions.question: Durgapur Steel Plant of West Bengal is situated on the banks of which river?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Damodar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Durgapur Steel Plant is located in Durgapur, West Bengal, and is one of the integrated steel plants of Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL).
 
• The plant is situated on the banks of the Damodar River, which is also known as the "Sorrow of Bengal" due to its history of flooding.
 
• Damodar River flows through the states of Jharkhand and West Bengal and is a significant water source for industrial operations, including steel production.
 
• The Durgapur Steel Plant was established in the late 1950s with assistance from the United Kingdom and has played a critical role in India's steel production sector.
 
• The Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC), a multipurpose river project, manages the water resources of the river to support industrial and irrigation needs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Teesta River:**

 
 
• The Teesta River flows through the Indian states of Sikkim and West Bengal and also enters Bangladesh.
 
• It originates from the Pahunri Glacier in the Himalayas and is known for its hydropower potential.
 
• Teesta is primarily used for irrigation and water supply in North Bengal but is not associated with steel plants like Durgapur.
 
 
 
• **Mahananda River:**
 
 
• Mahananda River flows through Bihar and West Bengal in India and enters Bangladesh.
 
• It is an important tributary of the Ganges River and supports agricultural activities in its basin.
 
• Mahananda does not play a role in industrial operations like steel production.
 
 
 
• **Hooghly River:**
 
 
• The Hooghly River is a distributary of the Ganges River and flows through West Bengal.
 
• It is significant for transportation, trade, and the operation of the Kolkata port, but it is not linked to Durgapur Steel Plant.
 
 
 
• **Damodar River and Steel Plants:**
 
 
• The Damodar River basin is rich in coal reserves, making it a hub for industrial activities, especially steel and thermal power production.
 
• Important steel plants such as Durgapur Steel Plant and Bokaro Steel Plant rely on the Damodar River for water resources.
 
• The river’s basin has been extensively developed for industrial and irrigation purposes under the Damodar Valley Corporation.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Judicial Review in India?

options.text: To examine the constitutionality of laws

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To examine the constitutionality of laws**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Judicial Review** in India refers to the power of the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of legislative enactments and executive orders.
 
• This power is derived from **Articles 13, 32, and 226** of the Indian Constitution, ensuring that laws and actions do not violate fundamental rights or the Constitution.
 
• The judiciary, particularly the Supreme Court and High Courts, have the authority to declare any law or act null and void if it is found to be unconstitutional.
 
• Judicial Review is a key feature of the **basic structure doctrine**, which was established by the Supreme Court in the **Keshavananda Bharati case (1973).**
 
• It acts as a system of checks and balances, ensuring that the legislative and executive branches function within their constitutional limits and uphold the rule of law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **To amend the Constitution (Option 2):**

 
 
• The power to amend the Constitution is provided under **Article 368** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Parliament has the authority to amend the Constitution, but this process requires a special majority in both houses and, in some cases, ratification by half of the state legislatures.
 
• Judicial Review cannot amend the Constitution; it is limited to ensuring the constitutionality of laws and actions.
 
 
 
• **To appoint ministers (Option 3):**
 
 
• The appointment of ministers is the responsibility of the **President of India**, as per Article 75 of the Constitution.
 
• The President appoints the Prime Minister and, on the advice of the Prime Minister, other ministers are appointed.
 
• This function does not fall under the scope of Judicial Review.
 
 
 
• **To elect judges (Option 4):**
 
 
• Judges in India are not elected but are appointed by the President under Articles 124 and 217 for the Supreme Court and High Courts, respectively.
 
• The appointment process involves consultation with the judiciary as per the **collegium system**.
 
• Judicial Review does not involve the election or appointment of judges.

questions.question: Within how many days must information be provided under the RTI Act for general requests?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**30 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under the Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005, public authorities are required to respond to RTI requests within **30 days** for general information.
 
• The RTI Act empowers citizens to request information from public authorities, ensuring transparency and accountability in government functioning.
 
• The timeline for providing information is strictly enforced, and failure to comply can lead to penalties for the Public Information Officer (PIO).
 
• If the information requested concerns the life or liberty of a person, the response time is reduced to **48 hours**.
 
• The RTI Act covers all constitutional authorities, including ministries, departments, and public sector undertakings, except intelligence and security organizations listed in the Second Schedule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **RTI Act Overview:**

 
 
• The RTI Act, enacted in 2005, aims to promote transparency and empower citizens to hold the government accountable.
 
• The Act defines processes for requesting information, appoints Public Information Officers (PIOs), and establishes penalties for non-compliance.
 
• Citizens can appeal to the Central Information Commission (CIC) or State Information Commission if their requests are denied or delayed.

questions.question: On which of the following dates did Mahatma Gandhi begin a 21-day fast of selfpurification to support the Harijan movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**May 08 1933.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi began his 21-day fast of self-purification on **May 8, 1933**, as part of his commitment to the Harijan movement.
 
• The fast aimed at promoting **social reform and the upliftment of Harijans (Dalits)**, advocating for the eradication of untouchability in India.
 
• This fast was a part of Gandhi’s broader vision of achieving social equality and justice as an integral element of India's freedom struggle.
 
• Gandhi believed that self-purification and personal penance were essential to inspire societal change and emphasize the moral foundation of his campaigns.
 
• The 21-day fast was one of the longest fasts undertaken by Mahatma Gandhi and demonstrated his unwavering commitment to nonviolence and social harmony.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harijan Movement**

 
 
• The Harijan movement, launched by Gandhi, aimed to abolish untouchability and integrate Dalits (Harijans) into mainstream society.
 
• He coined the term “Harijan,” meaning “children of God,” to address Dalits with dignity and respect.
 
• The movement emphasized access to education, public places, and temple entry for Harijans, challenging deeply entrenched social norms.
 
• It was a crucial part of Gandhi’s efforts to create a just and equitable society in pre-independent India.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT a part of the New Economic Policy reforms introduced in 1991?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nationalisation of banks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Nationalisation of banks** was not a part of the New Economic Policy (NEP) reforms introduced in 1991. Instead, nationalisation of banks occurred much earlier in India during 1969 and 1980.
 
• The NEP of 1991 focused on structural reforms aimed at liberalisation, globalisation, and privatisation to resolve the economic crisis.
 
• Unlike nationalisation, the NEP reforms sought to reduce government intervention in the economy and promote private sector participation.
 
• Under NEP, efforts were made to deregulate industries, reduce barriers to foreign investment, and promote competition instead of state-controlled monopolies.
 
• Nationalisation was primarily aimed at achieving socialistic goals like equitable distribution of resources, whereas NEP emphasised market-driven growth strategies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Liberalisation:**

 
 
• Liberalisation refers to the relaxation of government restrictions and regulations in areas like trade, industry, and investment.
 
• The NEP introduced significant liberalisation measures, such as abolishing the License Raj, reducing import tariffs, and encouraging foreign direct investment (FDI).
 
• The aim was to make the economy more efficient and competitive by allowing market forces to determine the allocation of resources.
 
 
 
• **Globalisation:**
 
 
• Globalisation involves integrating the domestic economy with the global economy by encouraging international trade and investment.
 
• The NEP facilitated globalisation by reducing trade barriers, allowing multinational corporations to operate in India, and adopting policies to attract foreign capital.
 
• This integration paved the way for technological advancements, improved infrastructure, and increased foreign exchange reserves.
 
 
 
• **Privatisation:**
 
 
• Privatisation refers to transferring ownership and control of state-owned enterprises to private entities.
 
• The NEP promoted privatisation by disinvesting in public sector undertakings (PSUs) and encouraging private sector participation in industries previously reserved for the public sector.
 
• Privatisation was aimed at improving efficiency, reducing fiscal burden, and stimulating economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Theme of New Economic Policy (NEP) 1991:**
 
 
• The NEP was introduced to address the balance of payments crisis and stagnation in economic growth.
 
• It marked a shift from a state-controlled economy to a market-driven economy.
 
• The three pillars of the NEP were liberalisation, privatisation, and globalisation, collectively known as LPG reforms.
 
• The NEP laid the foundation for India’s rapid economic growth in the subsequent decades.

questions.question: Who headed the Diwan-i-Arz and was responsible for managing soldiers, branding horses, and administering war provisions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ariz-i-Mumalik**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Ariz-i-Mumalik** was the head of the Diwan-i-Arz, the military department, during the Delhi Sultanate period.
 
• The main responsibilities of the Ariz-i-Mumalik included the **recruitment of soldiers**, ensuring the proper branding of horses, and maintaining war provisions.
 
• He was responsible for maintaining **discipline and order** within the military forces.
 
• He ensured the proper functioning of the army by organizing salaries, inspecting troops, and ensuring they were battle-ready.
 
• The Ariz-i-Mumalik was not involved in military strategy or commanding troops during war; his role was purely administrative and logistical.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Naib:**

 
 
• The Naib was the deputy or assistant to the Sultan and often acted as the **second-in-command** in the administrative hierarchy.
 
• In the absence of the Sultan, the Naib acted as the **regent** and handled the day-to-day functioning of the administration.
 
• The Naib often held significant power, sometimes even overshadowing the Sultan.
 
 
 
• **Amir-i-Dad:**
 
 
• The Amir-i-Dad was responsible for the administration of **justice** in the Sultanate.
 
• He ensured that the laws were implemented fairly and resolved disputes among the citizens.
 
• The Amir-i-Dad worked closely with the Qazi, the judicial officer, to uphold the legal system.
 
 
 
• **Dabir-i-Khas:**
 
 
• The Dabir-i-Khas was a **special secretary** to the Sultan, responsible for handling confidential and important correspondence.
 
• He played a crucial role in maintaining communication between the Sultan and other departments or foreign entities.
 
 
 
• **Diwan-i-Arz:**
 
 
• The Diwan-i-Arz was the **military department** of the Delhi Sultanate, tasked with managing the army and ensuring its preparedness.
 
• This department played a vital role in the administration of the Sultanate by ensuring efficient logistics, recruitment, and maintenance of military forces.

questions.question: How did globalisation impact Indian industries?

options.text: Gave more competition and modern technology

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gave more competition and modern technology**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Globalisation** introduced Indian industries to international markets, increasing competition and encouraging them to adopt modern technologies to stay competitive.
 
• It facilitated access to advanced technologies, better production methods, and innovative practices, leading to improved efficiency and productivity.
 
• Indian industries were exposed to global standards, pushing them to improve the quality of their products and services, thus making them globally competitive.
 
• Globalisation opened up foreign direct investment (FDI) opportunities, enabling Indian industries to collaborate with multinational companies for technology transfer and capital infusion.
 
• It also expanded the export potential of Indian industries, allowing them to tap into international markets and diversify their customer base.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Impact of Globalisation on Indian Industries**

 
 
• Globalisation refers to the integration of economies, societies, and cultures through international trade, investment, and technology.
 
• It brought both opportunities and challenges for Indian industries, compelling them to adapt and modernise.
 
• The sectors that benefited the most include IT, telecommunications, pharmaceuticals, and automotive industries.
 
• However, the unorganised sector and small-scale industries faced difficulties due to increased competition.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements correctly explains the cause of volcanism?

options.text: It results from molten rock rising from the Earth’s interior.
It is caused by excessive surface erosion.
It happens because of atmospheric disturbances.
It is due to the movement of glaciers.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It results from molten rock rising from the Earth's interior.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Volcanism occurs when molten rock, known as magma, rises from the Earth's mantle to the surface, driven by pressure differences and tectonic activity.
 
• At tectonic plate boundaries, such as divergent and convergent zones, magma can escape and form volcanic eruptions.
 
• The molten rock that reaches the surface is called lava, and it solidifies to create various landforms like volcanoes, lava domes, and plateaus.
 
• Volcanism is often associated with hotspots, where mantle plumes push magma to the surface, as seen in regions like Hawaii and Yellowstone.
 
• Volcanic eruptions contribute to the Earth's geological processes, including the formation of new crust, landforms, and mineral deposits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Excessive surface erosion**

 
 
• Surface erosion refers to the wearing away of the Earth’s surface due to wind, water, ice, or human activities.
 
• While erosion contributes to landscape changes, it does not cause volcanism, as volcanism is driven by processes within the Earth’s mantle and crust.
 
• Examples of erosion include river valleys, coastal cliffs, and desert landscapes, which are shaped by external forces rather than internal geological processes.
 
 
 
• ** Atmospheric disturbances**
 
 
• Atmospheric disturbances refer to weather phenomena such as storms, cyclones, or changes in air pressure.
 
• These events impact the atmosphere but do not influence volcanism, which originates from internal geological processes.
 
• Volcanic eruptions can affect the atmosphere, releasing gases like sulfur dioxide and ash clouds, but atmospheric phenomena cannot initiate volcanism.
 
 
 
• **Movement of glaciers**
 
 
• Glaciers are massive ice bodies that move slowly over land, shaping landscapes through processes like erosion and deposition.
 
• Glacial activity does not cause volcanism, as it is unrelated to the movement of magma or tectonic processes.
 
• However, glacial melting can sometimes interact with volcanic activity in regions like Iceland, where ice caps cover volcanic systems.

questions.question: Social life in the Vedic period was divided into how many ashramas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Four**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The concept of Ashramas was a fundamental part of social life during the Vedic period and was based on the division of an individual’s life into **four stages**.
 
• The four Ashramas were **Brahmacharya (student life)**, **Grihastha (householder life)**, **Vanaprastha (forest-dweller or hermit life)**, and **Sannyasa (renunciation)**.
 
• Each Ashrama represented a particular phase of life where an individual had specific duties and responsibilities to fulfill.
 
• The Ashrama system aimed at achieving individual spiritual growth while contributing to the betterment of society.
 
• It was primarily detailed in the **Dharmashastras** and other ancient texts like the Manusmriti, which provided guidelines for living a disciplined and virtuous life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Vedic Age (c. 1500-500 BCE) in ancient India, following the Indus Valley Civilization, is defined by the composition of the sacred Vedas and the Indo-Aryan culture, split into
 
 
• Early (1500-1000 BCE) and Later (1000-600 BCE) periods, transitioning from semi-nomadic pastoralism to settled agriculture, establishing foundational social structures (Varnas), and developing Vedic religion centered on rituals, soma, and fire sacrifices, with the Rigveda being the oldest text.

questions.question: Which statement best differentiates ROM from RAM in terms of volatility and usage?

options.text: RAM is volatile and stores temporary data; ROM is non-volatile and stores boot instructions
ROM is used for multitasking; RAM is used for storing BIOS.
ROM is volatile and used for running programs; RAM is non-volatile and stores firmware.
RAM is permanent; ROM is temporary.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RAM is volatile and stores temporary data; ROM is non-volatile and stores boot instructions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory)** is a volatile memory that temporarily stores data being used by the CPU during system operation.
 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory)** is non-volatile and retains data even when the computer is turned off.
 
• RAM is designed for high-speed data access and enables the smooth functioning of active applications and tasks.
 
• ROM stores critical data like the computer’s firmware or boot instructions, which are essential for initiating the system.
 
• RAM is writable and erasable, whereas ROM contains pre-written data that cannot be modified easily.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Volatile Memory (e.g., RAM)**

 
 
• Power: Needs continuous power to hold data.
 
• Speed: Very fast.
 
• Use: Temporary storage for running applications and active data.
 
• Examples: RAM (Random Access Memory), CPU Cache. 
 
 
 
• **Non-Volatile Memory (e.g., SSD, HDD)**
 
 
• Power: Retains data even without power.
 
• Speed: Slower than volatile memory.
 
• Use: Long-term storage for files, OS, software.
 
• Examples: SSDs, HDDs, USB drives, ROM (Read-Only Memory).

questions.question: The first session of the Indian National Congress was presided by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee** was the first president of the Indian National Congress (INC), which was established in 1885.
 
• The first session of the INC was held in **Bombay (now Mumbai)** from **December 28 to December 31, 1885**.
 
• He was a prominent lawyer and an influential political leader of his time.
 
• The first session was attended by **72 delegates**, marking the beginning of organized Indian political activism.
 
• Bonnerjee was instrumental in laying the foundation for the Congress, which later played a key role in India’s struggle for independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale:**

 
 
• He was an Indian political leader and social reformer during the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
 
• Gokhale was a senior leader of the Indian National Congress and a mentor to Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• He founded the **Servants of India Society** in 1905 to promote education and social reform.
 
 
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji:**
 
 
• Known as the **“Grand Old Man of India,”** he was the first Indian to be elected to the British Parliament.
 
• He was also a prominent leader of the INC and served as its president three times.
 
• Naoroji is well-known for his **Drain Theory**, which explained how Britain was exploiting India’s wealth.
 
 
 
• **Mahadev Govind Ranade:**
 
 
• He was a social reformer, scholar, and one of the early leaders of the Indian National Congress.
 
• Ranade advocated for modern education, women’s empowerment, and social reforms like the abolition of child marriage and caste discrimination.
 
• He was also a founding member of the **Prarthana Samaj**, a reformist movement in western India.

questions.question: Which of the following could be regarded as the only positive outcome of the British reforms in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Social reform laws**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The British reforms in India brought several **social reform laws** that aimed to eradicate regressive practices and promote progressive societal changes.
 
• These reforms included **abolition of practices like Sati** (widow immolation) through the Bengal Sati Regulation Act of 1829 under Lord William Bentinck.
 
• The British introduced laws to **prohibit child marriage**, such as the Child Marriage Restraint Act of 1929, which marked a significant step toward improving women's status.
 
• Efforts were made to ensure gender equality by passing legislation like the **Widow Remarriage Act of 1856**, which allowed widows to remarry and uplift their social condition.
 
• These social reforms laid the foundation for modern Indian society by addressing key issues like caste-based discrimination, untouchability, and improving education for women and marginalized groups.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deindustrialisation:**

 
 
• Deindustrialisation refers to the decline of traditional industries and handicrafts in India during British rule due to the influx of machine-made British goods.
 
• The British policies favored imports from Britain and heavily taxed Indian-made goods, leading to the destruction of local industries like textiles, especially in Bengal.
 
• This process caused massive unemployment and pushed artisans and craftsmen into poverty.
 
 
 
• **Ruralisation:**
 
 
• Ruralisation under British rule was characterized by the weakening of urban centers and the forced migration of skilled workers to villages due to the collapse of industries.
 
• The focus of British policies on agrarian revenue collection further contributed to ruralization, reducing the opportunities for urban economic development.
 
• It led to stagnation in rural areas and increased dependency on agriculture, often under exploitative systems like the zamindari system.
 
 
 
• **One-way free trade:**
 
 
• The British introduced policies promoting one-way free trade, allowing unrestricted import of British goods into India while restricting Indian exports.
 
• This led to a trade imbalance where Indian raw materials were exported to Britain, processed there, and sold back to India at higher prices.
 
• It was a strategy to make India a supplier of raw materials and a market for finished goods, which severely impacted India's economic structure.

questions.question: In February 2025, which Indian agency launched a ₹500-crore Technology Adoption Fund to support early-stage space startups and reduce import dependency?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IN-SPACe**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In February 2025, **IN-SPACe** (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Center) launched a ₹500-crore Technology Adoption Fund.
 
• The fund aims to support **early-stage space startups** in India by providing them with financial assistance and resources.
 
• It focuses on encouraging indigenization by reducing India’s **import dependency** in the space sector.
 
• IN-SPACe, established under the Department of Space, is responsible for promoting **private participation** in India’s space activities.
 
• This initiative aligns with the broader objective of making India a global hub for **space technology and innovation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Antrix Corporation**

 
 
• Antrix Corporation is the **commercial arm of ISRO** (Indian Space Research Organisation).
 
• It was established in 1992 and focuses on promoting and commercially exploiting products, technical consultancy services, and transfer of technologies developed by ISRO.
 
• Its core activities include satellite launches, transponder leasing, and satellite data sales.
 
 
 
• **ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation)**
 
 
• ISRO is the **space agency of the Government of India** and was founded in 1969.
 
• It is responsible for India’s space exploration and satellite development programs.
 
• ISRO has achieved milestones such as the **Chandrayaan missions, Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan)**, and Gaganyaan (India’s first human spaceflight program).
 
 
 
• **DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation)**
 
 
• DRDO is the **R&D wing of the Ministry of Defence**, established in 1958.
 
• It works on developing indigenous defense technologies like missiles, radars, and electronic warfare systems.
 
• While it plays a critical role in defense, it does not oversee space-related activities.

questions.question: The Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution was introduced through the 73rd Amendment. What is its significance in the context of Panchayati Raj?

options.text: It outlines administrative powers of the Gram Sabha.
It lists subjects to be legislated by the Union government
It specifies 29 functional subjects to be devolved to Panchayats by States.
It specifies 44 functional subjects to be devolved to Panchayats by States.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It specifies 29 functional subjects to be devolved to Panchayats by States**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Eleventh Schedule was introduced by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992, which aimed to strengthen the Panchayati Raj system in India.
 
• It contains a list of 29 subjects on which states can devolve powers and responsibilities to Panchayats for decentralized governance.
 
• The subjects include agriculture, irrigation, education, health, sanitation, social welfare, rural development, and others, emphasizing local self-governance.
 
• The Eleventh Schedule ensures that Panchayats have a defined role in the planning, implementation, and monitoring of development programs and schemes.

questions.question: What is the known equation that connects the concentration of a buffer solution's constituents, weak acid/salt or weak base/salt, and its pH?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Henderson-Hasselbalch equation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation is a mathematical representation used to calculate the pH of a buffer solution.
 
• The formula is: pH = pKa + log([A⁻]/[HA]), where [A⁻] represents the concentration of the conjugate base, and [HA] is the concentration of the weak acid.
 
• This equation demonstrates the relationship between the pH of a solution, the pKa (acid dissociation constant) of the weak acid, and the ratio of the concentrations of the conjugate base to the weak acid.
 
• The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation is commonly used in biochemistry and medicine to understand the behavior of buffer systems, such as maintaining blood pH levels.
 
• It is applicable for both acidic and basic buffer systems, making it a versatile tool in analytical chemistry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Arrhenius Equation**

 
 
• This equation describes the temperature dependence of reaction rates.
 
• The formula is: k = Ae^(-Ea/RT), where k is the rate constant, A is the frequency factor, Ea is the activation energy, R is the gas constant, and T is the temperature in Kelvin.
 
• It is widely used in physical chemistry to study reaction kinetics and the effect of temperature on chemical processes.
 
 
 
• **Nernst-Boyle Equation**
 
 
• This term is not recognized in scientific literature as a standard equation. The Nernst equation, however, is an important equation in electrochemistry.
 
• The Nernst equation calculates the electrochemical potential of a cell: E = E° - (RT/nF) * ln(Q), where E is the cell potential, E° is the standard cell potential, R is the gas constant, T is temperature, n is the number of moles of electrons, F is the Faraday constant, and Q is the reaction quotient.
 
 
 
• **Van't Hoff Equation**
 
 
• The Van't Hoff equation relates the change in equilibrium constant with temperature.
 
• The formula is: ln(K2/K1) = -ΔH/R * (1/T2 - 1/T1), where K1 and K2 are equilibrium constants at temperatures T1 and T2, ΔH is the enthalpy change, and R is the gas constant.
 
• This equation is used in thermodynamics to understand how temperature influences chemical equilibrium.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Buffer Solutions**

 
 
• A buffer solution is a system that resists changes in pH upon the addition of small amounts of acid or base.
 
• It typically consists of a weak acid and its conjugate base or a weak base and its conjugate acid.
 
• Buffer solutions are critical in maintaining the pH balance in biological systems, industrial applications, and chemical experiments.

questions.question: The retreating monsoon causes rainfall mainly in _____.

__
 
• The retreating monsoon, also known as the **northeast monsoon**, is responsible for bringing rainfall to Tamil Nadu and parts of the southeastern coast of India.
 
• This phenomenon occurs when the southwest monsoon winds retreat and are replaced by the dry, cool northeast winds.
 
• The period of retreating monsoon generally spans from **October to December**, which is also known as the "post-monsoon season."
 
• **Tamil Nadu receives about 48% of its annual rainfall** during the northeast monsoon season, making it a critical period for agriculture and water resources in the state.
 
• Coastal areas of Tamil Nadu, such as Chennai, experience significant rainfall due to the moisture-laden winds from the Bay of Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Assam**

 
 
• Assam primarily receives rainfall during the **southwest monsoon season** (June to September).
 
• It is located in the northeastern part of India and receives heavy rainfall due to the southwest monsoon winds that travel over the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Floods are a common occurrence in Assam during the monsoon season, especially in the Brahmaputra River basin.
 
 
 
• **Maharashtra**
 
 
• Maharashtra experiences rainfall mainly during the **southwest monsoon** (June to September).
 
• Regions like the Konkan coast, including Mumbai, receive heavy rainfall due to the orographic effect caused by the Western Ghats.
 
• The retreating monsoon does not contribute significantly to rainfall in Maharashtra.
 
 
 
• **Punjab**
 
 
• Punjab receives most of its rainfall during the **southwest monsoon** (July to September).
 
• The region also experiences occasional winter rainfall due to western disturbances originating from the Mediterranean region.
 
• The retreating monsoon has minimal impact on Punjab's rainfall patterns.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Retreating Monsoon**

 
 
• The retreating monsoon is characterized by the **withdrawal of the southwest monsoon winds** and the establishment of dry northeast trade winds.
 
• It marks the transition period between the wet monsoon season and the dry winter season.
 
• During this phase, the southern peninsula, particularly Tamil Nadu and parts of Andhra Pradesh, receives rainfall from the moisture-laden winds over the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Coastal cyclones are also common during this period, which can lead to heavy rainfall in southeastern India.

questions.question: In an optical fibre, the core is made of a _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**material with higher refractive index**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In an optical fibre, the core is made of a material with a **higher refractive index** than the cladding.
 
• This difference in refractive indices enables **total internal reflection**, which allows the light to propagate through the core without escaping.
 
• The core’s higher refractive index ensures that light entering at certain angles undergoes **continuous internal reflection**, making optical fibres highly efficient for transmitting light signals over long distances.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment has most recently extended the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for another ten years?

• The **104th Constitutional Amendment Act**, passed in January 2020, extended the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for another ten years, until January 2030.
 
• The original provision for reservation was introduced under Article 334 of the Indian Constitution and was set to expire after 70 years in January 2020. The 104th Amendment Act ensured its continuation.
 
• This amendment also abolished the reservation of seats for the Anglo-Indian community in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
 
• The reservation for SCs and STs is aimed at ensuring adequate representation for historically marginalized communities in India’s political decision-making process.
 
• The 104th Constitutional Amendment highlights the government’s commitment to social justice and equitable representation.

• The 15th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1963 was aimed at increasing the retirement age of High Court judges from 60 to 62 years.
 
• This amendment also provided provisions for compensatory allowances for judges transferring from one High Court to another.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment:**
 
 
• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 is also known as the "Mini Constitution" due to its extensive changes to the Constitution.
 
• It introduced the words "Socialist" and "Secular" in the Preamble and emphasized the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
 
 
• **61st Amendment:**
 
 
• The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988 reduced the voting age for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from 21 years to 18 years under Article 326.

questions.question: Shambhu Maharaj, awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship in 1967, was renowned for his contribution to which of the following Indian art forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak dance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Shambhu Maharaj** was a legendary Kathak dancer and teacher, recognized as one of the greatest exponents of the **Lucknow gharana** of Kathak.
 
• He was awarded the prestigious **Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship** in 1967 for his outstanding contribution to Indian classical dance.
 
• Kathak is a classical dance form from North India, characterized by intricate footwork, graceful movements, and storytelling through dance.
 
• Shambhu Maharaj’s mastery of **abhinaya (expression)** and his nuanced understanding of rhythm made him a prominent figure in the revival of Kathak in the 20th century.
 
• He trained many students and performed globally, ensuring the preservation and promotion of Kathak as a vital part of Indian cultural heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carnatic music:**

 
 
• Carnatic music is a classical music tradition from South India, known for its complex ragas (melodic frameworks) and talas (rhythmic cycles).
 
• It primarily involves vocal compositions accompanied by instruments like the veena, mridangam, and violin.
 
• Famous Carnatic musicians include Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Shyama Shastri, who are collectively known as the Trinity of Carnatic music.
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam dance:**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is deeply rooted in religious and spiritual themes, often depicting stories from Hindu mythology.
 
• The dance form is characterized by intricate hand gestures (mudras), facial expressions, and rhythmic footwork.
 
• Famous Bharatanatyam dancers include Rukmini Devi Arundale and Yamini Krishnamurthy.
 
 
 
• **Hindustani classical music:**
 
 
• Hindustani classical music is the traditional music of North India, distinct from Carnatic music of the South.
 
• It is based on ragas and talas, with instruments like the sitar, tabla, and sarod accompanying vocal performances.
 
• Prominent exponents include Ravi Shankar, Bismillah Khan, and Bhimsen Joshi.
 
 
 
• **Kathak dance:**
 
 
• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originating in the temples of North India.
 
• The dance form combines storytelling, intricate footwork, and spins, accompanied by classical music.
 
• Kathak is divided into three gharanas: Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras, each with its distinct style.
 
• Shambhu Maharaj belonged to the Lucknow gharana, which is known for its emphasis on grace and expression.

questions.question: What is the industrial name for calcium sulphate hemihydrate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plaster of Paris**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The industrial name for calcium sulphate hemihydrate is **Plaster of Paris (POP)**.
 
• It is chemically represented as **CaSO4·½H2O**, indicating that it contains half a molecule of water of crystallization.
 
• Plaster of Paris is produced by heating gypsum (calcium sulphate dihydrate) to about 150°C, which removes 75% of the water of hydration.
 
• It is widely used in construction, sculpture, and medical applications such as making molds, casts, and orthopedic supports due to its quick-setting property.
 
• When mixed with water, Plaster of Paris sets into a hard mass by reabsorbing water to form gypsum again, making it ideal for various applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gypsum**

 
 
• Gypsum is a naturally occurring mineral composed of calcium sulphate dihydrate (**CaSO4·2H2O**).
 
• It is the raw material used in the production of Plaster of Paris.
 
• Gypsum is primarily used in the construction industry to make drywall and plaster, as well as in agriculture as a soil conditioner.
 
• Unlike Plaster of Paris, gypsum contains two water molecules and does not harden quickly.
 
 
 
• **Quick Lime**
 
 
• Quick lime, also known as calcium oxide (**CaO**), is a white, caustic, and alkaline substance.
 
• It is produced by heating limestone (calcium carbonate) in a lime kiln to drive off carbon dioxide.
 
• Quick lime is used in the production of cement, steel, and paper and for water treatment and soil stabilization.
 
• It is not related to calcium sulphate or its derivatives such as Plaster of Paris.
 
 
 
• **Slaked Lime**
 
 
• Slaked lime, also known as calcium hydroxide (**Ca(OH)2**), is obtained by adding water to quick lime.
 
• It is widely used in construction for making mortar, whitewashing, and water purification.
 
• Slaked lime is chemically different from calcium sulphate hemihydrate and serves entirely different purposes.

• The name Dhaulagiri comes from Sanskrit, meaning “White Mountain,” due to its snow-covered peak.

• The peak was first summited in 1953 by Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay.
 
• Everest is known locally as “Sagarmatha” in Nepal and “Chomolungma” in Tibet.

• It is located in Pakistan-administered Kashmir (POK), making it **outside Indian territory**.
 
• Known as the “Killer Mountain” due to its high fatality rate among climbers, it was first summited by Austrian climber Hermann Buhl in 1953.
 
• The name “Nanga Parbat” translates to “Naked Mountain” in Urdu, referring to its bare rock and ice faces.

questions.question: In May 2024, the World Health Organization (WHO) prequalified the QDENGA vaccine developed by Takeda Pharmaceuticals. This vaccine is designed to protect against which disease?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dengue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• QDENGA is a tetravalent dengue vaccine developed by Takeda Pharmaceuticals and approved by the World Health Organization (WHO) in May 2024.
 
• The vaccine is effective against all four serotypes of the dengue virus (DEN-1, DEN-2, DEN-3, and DEN-4).
 
• Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease primarily transmitted through the bite of infected Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes.
 
• QDENGA is targeted at reducing the global burden of dengue, which infects approximately 390 million people annually, with severe cases potentially leading to death.
 
• The vaccine is particularly beneficial for endemic regions, where dengue outbreaks cause significant morbidity and strain on healthcare systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Malaria:**

 
 
• Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites and transmitted through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
 
• The WHO-recommended malaria vaccine is RTS,S/AS01 (brand name: Mosquirix), which targets Plasmodium falciparum, the deadliest malaria parasite.
 
• Efforts to combat malaria also include insecticide-treated bed nets, indoor spraying, and anti-malarial medicines.
 
 
 
• **Chikungunya:**
 
 
• Chikungunya is a viral disease transmitted through Aedes mosquitoes, the same vectors responsible for dengue transmission.
 
• The disease is characterized by fever and severe joint pain, which can persist for months or years in some cases.
 
• There is currently no specific vaccine or antiviral treatment for chikungunya; management focuses on symptom relief.
 
 
 
• **Zika:**
 
 
• Zika virus is another mosquito-borne disease transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, with symptoms including mild fever, rash, and conjunctivitis.
 
• It is particularly concerning for pregnant women, as it can lead to microcephaly and other congenital abnormalities in newborns.
 
• No vaccine is currently available for Zika, and prevention focuses on mosquito control and personal protection.
